relevance_note: A 24-patient paediatric PID cohort with one individually described TNFAIP3 carrier: 'Genetic analysis revealed a heterozygous c.259C>T mutation in TNFAIP3, indicating an A20 deficiency.'
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; values typed in a small Python script and every span checked verbatim by script. Only Patient #18 (the single TNFAIP3 carrier) is in scope; the other 23 cohort patients (variants in other genes or none) get no rows and are counted in cohort_size_as_stated (24). Label 'Patient #18' is the text's form ('Patient #18'); Table 2 prints '#18'. Table 2 column 'A' is defined in the legend as age at the time of diagnosis (months), so 192 is recorded as age at diagnosis (P192M); no onset or last-evaluation age is given. Table 2 '-' cells (Physical findings, Additional manifestations) have no legend definition, so nothing is excluded from them; 'ND' is defined as not done. The Discussion sentence 'Our patient had hypogammaglobulinemia, colitis, ileitis...' is attributed to Patient #18 because it names the same TNFAIP3 c.259C>T variant. 'AD' means autoinflammatory disorders in Table 2's legend but antibody deficiency in Table 3's legend (inconsistency in the paper; not relevant to #18's row values). The authors call the variant a 'mutation' only; no classification, protein change, transcript, inheritance or parental testing is given. Lymphonodular hyperplasia was not mapped to the checklist item 'lymphoproliferation or lymphadenopathy' (left not reported). n_patients_reported=1 is derived from the paper naming one TNFAIP3 patient; the authors do not state the number as a count. Table 2 also prints a duplicated #9 row (not in scope). No stacked cells.
